biomarkers.name: T-cell immunophenotype (cCD3, CD5, CD7, CD1a, CD4, CD8, TdT)
biomarkers.clinical_use: cCD3 is lineage-defining. TdT+ distinguishes from mature T-cell leukaemia/lymphoma

biomarkers.name: NOTCH1 mutations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common driver; often associated with favorable-risk biology, particularly when accompanied by FBXW7 mutation in some risk models. γ-secretase inhibitors remain investigational

biomarkers.name: FBXW7 mutations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Often co-occurring with NOTCH1; in some treatment contexts may associate with favorable prognosis

biomarkers.name: Molecular subtypes (TAL/LMO, HOXA, TLX1, TLX3)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Distinct biology; TAL1/LMO-deregulated cases are common, especially in adults

biomarkers.name: MRD (flow, NGS)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Post-induction and post-consolidation MRD is a major risk-stratification tool and may guide transplant decisions

biomarkers.name: Nelarabine
biomarkers.clinical_use: T-cell-active chemotherapy used in T-ALL/T-LBL, particularly in relapsed/refractory disease and in some frontline regimens; not a validated biomarker

biomarkers.name: Recurrent transcription factor rearrangements (TAL1, TLX1, TLX3, LMO1, LMO2, HOXA, NKX2-1/NKX2-2, MEF2C, MYB)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Hallmark drivers of T-ALL biology that define molecular subgroups and developmental arrest states

biomarkers.name: CDKN2A/CDKN2B deletions
biomarkers.clinical_use: Very common secondary lesions in T-ALL; contribute to leukemogenesis and risk stratification in some studies

biomarkers.name: PTEN / PI3K-AKT pathway alterations
biomarkers.clinical_use: Recurrent lesions associated with pathway activation and potential therapeutic relevance

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Lymphoblasts with T-cell immunophenotype (cCD3+, TdT+); often presents with anterior mediastinal mass in adolescents/young adults
variants: T-lymphoblastic lymphoma (classically <25% marrow blasts with mass-dominant disease)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Not graded; molecular subtypes and MRD drive management

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Emerging CD5- and CD7-directed CAR-T strategies in trials; more challenging than B-cell targeting because of T-cell fratricide
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Marrow and thymic-mass infiltration; extramedullary sites include mediastinum, lymph nodes, spleen

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: T-cell precursors arrested at thymic developmental stage — cortical thymocyte is common, although cases span early/pro-T through more mature thymic stages
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: T-cell lineage assignment (cCD3+, CD7+, TdT+) with maturation arrest at various thymic developmental stages: pro-T, pre-T, cortical thymocyte, medullary thymocyte; cortical thymocyte arrest is common (often CD4+CD8+ double positive with CD1a+)
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: T-cell developmental hierarchy dictates immunophenotype; NOTCH1 pathway activation is a central driver in many cases, while TAL1, LMO1/2, TLX1, TLX3, HOXA-related lesions and other transcription factor deregulation define distinct maturation arrest patterns
